chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Adam (peace be upon him) was sent down from Paradise to Al-Safa, and Hawwa (peace be upon him) to Al-Marwa, and she had been combing her hair in Paradise with perfume from the perfumes of Paradise. So when she came to be on earth, she said: 'What hope is there for me in combing, while I am loathsome to my hair?' So she loosened her braids, and from her combing which she used to comb with in Paradise, there scattered [particles], and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hassan – similar to it.

He said: 'And in another Hadith: She loosened her braids, so Allah sent upon what was therein from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the East and the West. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* links the physical origin of perfume to the Fall of Hawwa, interpreting the scattering of her hair's perfume as a divine distribution of blessings across the earth, particularly to India. It reflects the Shia tradition of connecting earthly phenomena to primordial events in Paradise, offering a spiritual dimension to material goods. The hadith also includes a variant where the wind distributes the scent globally, emphasizing the universal nature of this divine gift.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Adamas descended from the Paradise upon Al-Safa and Hawwaas upon the Marwa, and sheas used to comb in the Paradise with a perfume from the perfumes of the Paradise.

So when she<sup>as</sup> came to be in the earth, she<sup>as</sup> said: ‘How hopeful I<sup>as</sup> am from the combing and I<sup>as</sup> am loathsome of my<sup>as</sup> hair’. So she<sup>as</sup> loosened her<sup>as</sup> braids, so there scattered from her combing which she<sup>as</sup> used to comb with in the Paradise, and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India’.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Adullah, from Ali Bin Hassan – similar to it.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And in another Hadeeth - : 
‘She<sup>as</sup> loosened her braids, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent upon what was therein, from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the eat and the west. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Hassan from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When Adam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, came down from the garden (paradises) at al-Safa’ and Eve on al-Marwah, she wore a hairstyle from the garden (paradise) with the perfume of the garden (paradise). When she turned on earth she said, ‘I have no hope in this hairstyling while I am being angered at.’ She opened her braid. The perfume from her hairstyling that she had done in the garden (paradises) spread and the wind blew it away. The majority of it fell in India, thus perfume is in India.”’
A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘ Abd Allah from Ali ibn Hassan a similar Hadith.
In another Hadith it is said that ‘. . . ‘her braid’ . . . ‘ Allah sent on what was there (in her braid) of perfumes a wind which blew to the east and west, thus the origin of perfume is thereof.
